 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain

Misc. Criminal Case No. 24429 of 2025
 Prabhat Kumar Soni
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
Shri Sameer Kumar Shrivastava, learned counsel and Shri  Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Harish Sharma, learned Public Prosecu  respondent/State.

ORDER The present application has been filed for grant of anticipatory bail under section 482 of BNSS by the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.87 of 2025 registered at Police Station Lahar, District Bhind for the offences punishable under sections 420, 409/34 of IPC.

2. It is contended by counsel for applicant that the allegations in the matter are arising out of money transaction and as per contents of FIR, one Atul Soni, who was the Director of M/s Vishnupatni Udyog Pvt. Ltd., had entered into some agreement with two firms owned by the complainant, even as per FIR allegations, the business was carried out by Atul Soni and Amit Soni, who managed the company i.e. M/s Vishnupatni Udyog Pvt. Ltd. on one side and the complainant on other side and on account of substandard NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:11697 2 MCRC-24429-2025 supply of the goods on various consignment the total loss was to the complainant to the tune of rupees fifteen crore, which after the enquiry was found to the tune of Rs.3.31 crore.
It is contended that Atul Soni has already been arrested and the present applicant is roped in the matter only because he is brother-in-law of Atul Soni.
It is contended that in the FIR there are no specific allegations against the present applicant and only one line has been written that he is accomplice of Atul Soni.
He is an employee of HDFC Bank and was not associated with the said company, with which business transaction was going in between his brother-in-law being Director of the company.

It is further argued that the goods were supplied from Indore to Delhi and Noida and apart from the complainant having been native of Lahar, District Bhind, no ingredients of any crime being committed at Lahar are made out and considering these facts also the benefit of anticipatory bail may be granted to the present applicant.

sentences.text:
Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by learned counsel for the State on the ground that on the basis of memorandum under Section 27 of Evidence Act of co-accused Mohit Tadvate and Atul Soni that has been taken and as per the said memorandum, the present applicant used to look after the bank related work of the company, therefore, it is contended that the present applicant has not made out any case for grant of anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
4.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to grant the benefit of anticipatory bail to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:11697 3 MCRC-24429-2025 applicant, though with stringent conditions, but without commenting anything on the merits of the case.
5.

Accordingly, this application is allowed and it is directed that in case, if the applicant appears before the Investigating Officer/trial Court within fifteen days from today and furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer/trial Court, in the event of arrest, he shall be released on anticipatory bail.

It is made clear that in case if applicant fails to appear before the Investigating Officer/trial Court within the fifteen days from today, then this order shall automatically stand cancelled.
6.
